_readme: Why this file exists: the site is in Thai, the knowledge base is in Thai, and
essentially every real visitor will type Thai. But the rules are written in
English and every case in cases.json is English. A guardrail proven in a
language nobody uses is not proven.
Thai has no spaces between words, so substring assertions need care: a short
Thai fragment can appear inside an unrelated word. Patterns here are chosen
to be long enough to be unambiguous, and 'none' patterns still follow the
English rule - they must be constructible only in the affirmative.
These are the highest-severity rules only (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 12). Style and
scope cases are not repeated: a style slip in Thai is cosmetic, an
immigration-advice breach in Thai is the same harm as in English.
